title: Reading French news without a dictionary
description: Read a short original French news text about a fusion record at Cadarache and the ITER worksite, and discover how much you understand through look-alike words, numbers, names and context.

sources.title: EUROfusion: World record fusion plasma in Europe (CEA news)
sources.note: WEST at CEA Cadarache held a plasma for 1,337 seconds on 12 February 2025 (plasma 61299), 25 % longer than the record set in China a few weeks earlier; 2 MW of lower hybrid heating.

sources.title: Connaissance des énergies (AFP): Fusion nucléaire, le CEA annonce un record mondial de durée de plasma en France, 18 February 2025
sources.note: The record on 12 February 2025, announced on 18 February; about 22 minutes; a plasma of several tens of millions of degrees; the earlier record set in China in January. Used only to check the facts: the lesson's text is original.

sources.title: WEST (formerly Tore Supra) (Wikipedia)
sources.note: WEST is the CEA's tokamak at Cadarache; 1,337 s on 12 February 2025.

sources.title: ITER Organization: What will ITER do?
sources.note: 500 MW of fusion power from 50 MW of input heating power (Q = 10).

sources.title: ITER press release: two-thirds of the tokamak core in place, 29 July 2026 (PDF)
sources.note: The sixth of nine sector modules lowered into the tokamak pit on 28 July 2026, almost six months ahead of schedule; the last one planned for mid-2027.

sources.title: ITER (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Seven members; 2024 baseline: start of research operation 2034.

sources.title: ITER Organization: ITER France
sources.note: The PACA International School in Manosque began in 2007 with 130 pupils aged 3 to 18; six language sections and a European section; France committed to bilingual education as host.

sources.title: Nombres en français (Wikipédia): milliard, billion
sources.note: French uses the long scale: un milliard = 10^9, un billion = 10^12.

sources.title: False friend (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Words that look alike in two languages but differ in meaning.
